chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is not correct for the man to wear silk except during the battle.
ai.seo_question: When is it permissible for men to wear silk according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the general prohibition of silk for men by introducing a specific functional exception for warfare, likely referring to its use for protection or identification in battle. This ruling aligns with the broader Shia jurisprudential understanding that prohibitions can be lifted for necessity (darurah) or specific utility, distinguishing between luxury and practical application.
